classification.conformanceProfile: RFC 3533 Ogg + Vorbis I bounded single-logical-stream audio profile; RFC 5334 audio/ogg codecs=vorbis

formatPolicy.playbackBoundaryAuthority: Vorbis granule-position semantics as interpreted by the Xiph reference decoder and corroborated by an exact external technical view
formatPolicy.browserBoundaryPolicy: Browser decoders must successfully decode and expose the contracted rate/channel topology; sample-boundary equality across browser engines is observed and reported, not assumed by profile PASS

contractSchema.claim: Ogg Vorbis object contract is valid under audio-ogg-vorbis-contract-v1

oggVorbisIntegrity.claim: Xiph ogginfo accepts exactly one completed Vorbis logical stream with version 0 and contract rate/channel facts

referenceDecode.claim: Xiph oggdec decodes canonical signed little-endian 16-bit PCM whose per-channel sample count equals the contract playback boundary

independentTechnicalView.claim: FFprobe independently identifies one Ogg/Vorbis stream and exposes contract rate/channel/playback-duration facts

independentDecodeObservation.claim: FFmpeg independently decodes the stream and its common canonical s16le prefix remains numerically compatible with the Xiph reference output; decoder-specific priming/end-boundary differences are reported rather than redefined as standard semantics

browserTargetMatrix.claim: Pinned Chromium and Firefox both decode the exact Ogg/Vorbis bytes at the contracted rate/channel topology; decoded sample-boundary agreement is explicitly reported

nonClaims: bit-exact PCM equality across independent Vorbis decoder implementations
factual or artistic correctness of the audio content
subjective sound quality, loudness or mastering quality
truth or completeness of Vorbis comments/tags
support for chained or multiplexed Ogg logical streams
Game suitability beyond the consuming Game's own acceptance
rights or licensing validity of encoded content
